correctness.rationale: The paired-letter Parikh difference random walk gives an iff condition for every short Abelian border, including the correct even central and odd middle cases. The multinomial-squared generating function counts all q-ary return walks; first-return decomposition proves both exact bivariate series. Their specialization \(v=1\) matches all \(q^n\) words. A multinomial local CLT with covariance determinant \(q^{-q}\) gives \(p_{q,j}\sim q^{q/2}/(4\pi j)^{(q-1)/2}\); exact factorial-moment convolution bounds prove the exponential ternary law, Dirichlet moments recover the binary benchmark, and finite escape probability yields the geometric law in \(q\ge4\). Actual verifier script returns VERIFY_OK for exhaustive direct words and two independently constructed coefficient computations.

value.rationale: The next natural case beyond the published binary complete-multiplicity theorem is not a small numerical increment: the rank of the difference walk changes and produces a trichotomy. All word lengths and all proper-border multiplicities over every alphabet have a computable exact bivariate enumerator. For \(q=3\), the short-border multiplicity diverges logarithmically with a proved exponential law and explicit sharp constant 3 sqrt(3)/(4 pi); for \(q\ge4\) it stays geometrically bounded. These structurally different distributions are not obtained from mere binary counts or the presence/absence of a border and are of direct use for random-word Abelian-border statistics.
